key_insight: The paper derives first-principles interfacial jump conditions for premixed flames in Darcy-flow media, showing that finite flame thickness, nonunity Lewis number, heat loss, and gravity introduce distinct Markstein corrections and a new flame-dispersion relation.
engineering_relevance: This gives a more rigorous predictive model for flame stability and propagation in porous media and Hele-Shaw channels, improving design and interpretation of confined combustion systems.
method: Systematic multiple-scale analysis to derive interfacial conditions
Closed-form Markstein numbers and dispersion relation under Darcy's law
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an analytical derivation with explicit formulas and a new dispersion relation, rather than a data-driven validation or numerical benchmark.
watch_item: The theory is asymptotic and interface-based, so accuracy may degrade when flames are not thin or when transport/geometry effects fall outside Darcy-flow assumptions.
paper_title: Hydrodynamic theory of premixed flames under Darcy's law: Interfacial conditions and effects of nonunity Lewis number and heat loss
